texts.text: W3C issues press release about developing Verifiable Credential Barcodes

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Published on: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:50:00 +0000
texts.text: Published on: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:50:00 +0000

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In a press release we present the concept of real-time revocation that is being developed in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Barcodes specification to protect physical documents.
texts.text: In a press release we present the concept of real-time revocation that is being developed in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Barcodes specification to protect physical documents.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Recently the data theft of approximately 160 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada was reported and unfortunately, identity thieves will use this data to impersonate victims. Real-time revocation is needed to protect individuals against identity theft. The future of physical document security is being decided as we speak. W3C Verifiable Credential Barcodes are the solution - and the technology is open and free for all to use. The Verifiable Credential Barcodes technology we are building in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Working Group is already protecting millions of people from identity theft and fraud, with the potential to protect billions more. We want to make sure that government organizations and policymakers know that there is a free and open solution to this problem that is being designed for the public good.

texts.text: The [SVG Working Group](https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/svg/) invites implementations of an updated Candidate Recommendation Snapshot of [Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CR-SVG2-20261006/).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This is a fresh version of SVG2 with corrections, clarifications and improvements for more interoperability, in particular in implementations in web browsers.
texts.text: This is a fresh version of SVG2 with corrections, clarifications and improvements for more interoperability, in particular in implementations in web browsers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This specification defines the features and syntax for Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) Version 2. SVG is a language based on XML for describing two-dimensional vector and mixed vector/raster graphics. SVG content is stylable, scalable to different display resolutions, and can be viewed stand-alone, mixed with HTML content, or embedded using XML namespaces within other XML languages. SVG also supports dynamic changes; script can be used to create interactive documents, and animations can be performed using declarative animation features or by using script.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The W3C Board of Directors is the governing body of the Consortium. The Board has ultimate authority on its strategic direction, has legal obligations and fiduciary responsibility over W3C as a whole. Directors are formally responsible for the correct running of the organization; this is generally characterized in three broad "fiduciary" duties: (1) a duty of care (to exercise good business judgment of a reasonable person with their experience); (2) duty of loyalty (to serve the best interest of the organization); and (3) a duty of obedience (in accordance with all applicable laws and rules). W3C Board of Directors seats are non-paid positions. Learn more about the [W3C Board of Directors responsibilities](https://www.w3.org/2024/06/w3c-board-of-directors-skills-description.html).

texts.orig: Published on: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:13:00 +0000

texts.label: text
texts.orig: W3C is pleased to announce the report from the W3C Workshop on the Future of ODRL, held in July 2026 in London, UK, and online.
texts.text: W3C is pleased to announce the report from the W3C Workshop on the Future of ODRL, held in July 2026 in London, UK, and online.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: W3C is pleased to announce the [report](https://www.w3.org/2026/ODRLWS/report.html) from the [W3C Workshop on the Future of ODRL](https://www.w3.org/2026/ODRLWS/index.html), held in July 2026 in London, UK, and online.
texts.text: W3C is pleased to announce the [report](https://www.w3.org/2026/ODRLWS/report.html) from the [W3C Workshop on the Future of ODRL](https://www.w3.org/2026/ODRLWS/index.html), held in July 2026 in London, UK, and online.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Bringing together participants from standards organizations, industry, academia and the broader policy, data and rights communities, the workshop covered media, core semantics, banking and finance, data spaces, legal and regulatory applications, and new language features. It was explicitly positioned as a turning point for ODRL.
texts.text: Bringing together participants from standards organizations, industry, academia and the broader policy, data and rights communities, the workshop covered media, core semantics, banking and finance, data spaces, legal and regulatory applications, and new language features. It was explicitly positioned as a turning point for ODRL.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The emerging vision is considerably broader than simply producing another revision of the ODRL vocabulary. There was consensus to establish a new W3C ODRL Working Group set to work on ODRL 3.0 as a foundation for machine-readable, interoperable and increasingly machine-actionable policies, capable of operating across sectors and integrating with complementary standards for identity, provenance, legal information, data spaces and digital contracts.
texts.text: The emerging vision is considerably broader than simply producing another revision of the ODRL vocabulary. There was consensus to establish a new W3C ODRL Working Group set to work on ODRL 3.0 as a foundation for machine-readable, interoperable and increasingly machine-actionable policies, capable of operating across sectors and integrating with complementary standards for identity, provenance, legal information, data spaces and digital contracts.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The workshop's outcomes can be distilled into the following principal recommendations:
texts.text: The workshop's outcomes can be distilled into the following principal recommendations:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Establish the new W3C ODRL 3.0 Working Group
texts.text: Establish the new W3C ODRL 3.0 Working Group

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Start with use cases and explicit requirements
texts.text: Start with use cases and explicit requirements

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Strengthen the formal semantics of ODRL
texts.text: Strengthen the formal semantics of ODRL

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Define conformance for policy-processing software
texts.text: Define conformance for policy-processing software

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Develop a comprehensive conformance test suite
texts.text: Develop a comprehensive conformance test suite

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Adopt modular and potentially multi-level conformance
texts.text: Adopt modular and potentially multi-level conformance

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Improve usability
texts.text: Improve usability

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Position ODRL as an interoperability layer
texts.text: Position ODRL as an interoperability layer

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Investigate integration with complementary standards

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The workshop's closing discussion confirmed that the workshop chairs would draft a Working Group charter. The intention is to socialize the charter at [TPAC 2026](https://www.w3.org/news-events/tpac/2026/) in Dublin, with the objective of moving into the next phase of ODRL 3.0 by the end of 2026.

This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users. Conceptually, one or more public key credentials, each scoped to a given WebAuthn Relying Party, are created by and bound to authenticators as requested by the web application. The user agent mediates access to authenticators and their public key credentials in order to preserve user privacy. Authenticators are responsible for ensuring that no operation is performed without user consent. Authenticators provide cryptographic proof of their properties to Relying Parties via attestation. This specification also describes the functional model for WebAuthn conformant authenticators, including their signature and attestation functionality. texts.text: The Profiles Vocabulary is an RDF vocabulary created to allow the machine-readable description of profiles of specifications for information resources.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The [Dataset Exchange Working Group](https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/dx) has published today a First Public Working Draft of [The Profiles Vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-dx-prof-1.0-20260820/). The Profiles Vocabulary is an RDF vocabulary created to allow the machine-readable description of profiles of specifications for information resources. It can be used to describe profile hierarchies wherein profiles of specifications may themselves have profiles indicated. It can also be used to link together multiple profile resources that make up a profile - guidelines, validation tools, schemas, term lists and so on - and it allows for those profile resources to be described with formats, roles, and digital artifacts.

Decentralized identifier (DID) resolution is the process of obtaining a DID document and accompanying metadata for a specific DID. A resolved DID document is a set of information which enables cryptographically verifiable interactions with the DID subject, including mechanisms such as cryptographic public keys.

texts.orig: This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users.
texts.text: This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Today, the W3C Team proposed advancing [Web Authentication: An API for accessing Public Key Credentials Level 3](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CR-webauthn-3-20260526/) to W3C Recommendation. This specification was published by the [Web Authentication Working Group](https://www.w3.org/groups/wg/webauthn/) as a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot on 26 May 2026. This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users. Conceptually, one or more public key credentials, each scoped to a given WebAuthn Relying Party, are created by and bound to authenticators as requested by the web application. The user agent mediates access to authenticators and their public key credentials in order to preserve user privacy. Authenticators are responsible for ensuring that no operation is performed without user consent. Authenticators provide cryptographic proof of their properties to Relying Parties via attestation. This specification also describes the functional model for WebAuthn conformant authenticators, including their signature and attestation functionality.
